title: Inspector General Eko Hadi Dismissed in Prabowo Wiretapping Case, Admits Regret and Apologizes
text:
Inspector General Eko Hadi Dismissed in Prabowo Wiretapping Case, Admits Regret and Apologizes 
 SKANDAL PENYADAPAN Inspector General Eko Hadi Dismissed in Prabowo Wiretapping Case, Admits Regret and Apologizes
 Eko Hadi Santoso has been found guilty of conspiring to engage in illegal access activities, specifically wiretapping, by unprofessionally utilizing technology owned by the National Police.
 17 Nov 2026 21:27 WIB · Politik & Hukum 
 DOK. POLRI TV
 Kecil Sedang Besar Sangat Besar Share
 Copy Link
 By Norbertus Arya Dwiangga Martiar 
 This article has been translated using AI. See original . 
 00:00 00:00 10 10 1.00x JAKARTA, KOMPAS - Following the dismissal of Inspector General Ahrie Sonta Nasution, Inspector General Eko Hadi Santoso has now been removed from his position in the National Police without honor due to his involvement in the wiretapping of President Prabowo Subianto and several other figures. While expressing regret and offering an apology, Eko Hadi Santoso immediately announced his intention to appeal the decision made by the Police Professional Ethics Commission.
 The hearing of the Police Professional Ethics Code Commission (KKEP) against Inspector General Eko Hadi Santoso took place in the courtroom of the Police Division of Profession and Security at the National Police Headquarters, Building 3, Second Floor, on Tuesday (17/11/2026). The session ran from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM WIB.
 The Head of the Public Information Bureau of the National Police's Public Relations Division, Brigadier General Trunoyudo Wisnu Andiko, stated that the hearing was led by Commissioner General Hendro Pandowo, Vice Chairman of the Commission Irjen Agus Dwi Hermawan, along with Commission members Irjen Untung Widyatmoko, Irjen Arie Ardian Rishadi, and Irjen Toni Ariadi Efendi.
 Nine witnesses testified, including Dr.
 From the trial, Eko Hadi Santoso was proven to have made an agreement regarding illegal access activities in the form of wiretapping using access or technological tools belonging to the Police in an unprofessional and unprocedural manner.
 The person concerned violated Article 13 Paragraph 1 of Government Regulation (PP) Number 1 of 2003 concerning Dismissal of Members of the Indonesian National Police in conjunction with Article 5 Paragraph 1 letter b and/or Article 5 Paragraph 1 letter c, and/or Article 8 letter c number 1, and/or Article 10 paragraph 1 letter d, and/or Article 10 paragraph 1 letter f, and/or Article 11 paragraph 1 letter a, and/or Article 11 paragraph 1 letter b of Police Regulation Number 7 of 2022 concerning the Professional Code of Ethics and the Indonesian National Police Code of Ethics Commission as amended by Police Regulation Number 4 of 2026.
 As a result of his actions, the Police Professional Ethics Code Commission imposed an ethical sanction declaring the violator's behavior as disgraceful. "Secondly, there is an administrative sanction, which is the Dishonorable Dismissal or PTDH from the police force," said Trunoyudo.
 In response to the ruling, Eko Hadi Santoso announced his intention to appeal. The case will proceed through the appeals process and will be handled by the appeals commission, as stipulated in Article 69 of Police Regulation Number 7 of 2022 concerning the Code of Professional Ethics and the Police Ethics Commission.
 M Choirul Anam, a member of the National Police Commission (Kompolnas), stated that during the hearing, all parties were given the opportunity to elaborate, present their interests, outline their authority, recount events, and share the facts they experienced. He noted that the construction of events within the framework of the ethics hearing had been thoroughly detailed.
 The presence of mitigating witnesses has led to a lengthy interaction and defense process. Similarly, the prosecution of Eko has also been quite extensive.
 Not only that, said Anam, Eko Hadi expressed regret and apologized during the trial, even though he later filed an appeal.
 "We believe that the mechanism that took place earlier was conducted in accordance with the regulations, and Kompolnas considers that the credibility of the event and the mechanism that was organized has been maintained," Anam stated.
 Eko Hadi Santoso is a senior officer who graduated from the Police Academy in 1999. At the time he was named a suspect, he held the position of Senior Police Instructor at the Level I Sespim Lemdiklat Polri. Previously, he served as the Director of Drug Crimes at the National Police Criminal Investigation Agency.
 Eko has become the second high-ranking officer in the National Police to face dismissal (PTDH) in connection with the alleged illegal wiretapping of President Prabowo Subianto. On Tuesday (10/11/2026), Inspector General Ahrie Sonta was dismissed earlier during a KKEP hearing. Ahrie Sonta has also announced his intention to appeal the decision.
 Listyo Sigit's ethics hearing 
 In addition to Eko Hadi and Ahrie Sonta, other senior police officers who have been named suspects in the illegal wiretapping of President Prabowo include former National Police Chief General (Pol) Listyo Sigit Prabowo and Inspector General Slamet Uliandi. They will also face an ethics trial conducted by the KKEP.
 The KKEP hearing for Listyo Sigit is scheduled to take place next week. Trunoyudo confirmed that the ethical hearing will be conducted in accordance with Article 42, Paragraph (3) of Police Regulation Number 7 of 2022 concerning the Code of Professional Ethics and the Police Ethics Commission. This regulation states that the membership composition of the KKEP must consist of individuals with the same or higher rank than that of the alleged violator.
 "We will convey this later in accordance with the Perpol mechanism that we conveyed earlier," said Trunoyudo.
 Slamet Uliandi has yet to attend the ethics hearing due to his health condition, reportedly suffering from post-stroke complications. This health issue has also resulted in Slamet not being detained, unlike the three other suspects.
 The Head of the Public Relations Division of the National Police, Inspector General Johnny Eddizon Isir, stated that the ethical hearing for Slamet was not forced to take place as a form of respect for human rights. "On one hand, we must continue to respect human rights, considering the health condition of the alleged violator, SU (Slamet Uliandi)," he said.
